marble.name: 10 More or 10 Less
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Mentally find 10 more or 10 less than a given two-digit number without counting
marble.prompt: Can you quickly tell you what is 10 more than 43 or 10 less than 71 — without counting up or down one at a time?

cluster.summary: Your child is building number foundations — learning to read and write numbers up to 100, understanding number words, and beginning to see how numbers are built from tens and ones.

misconceptions: Counting on in ones (56, 57, 58…66) instead of jumping a ten — no place-value shortcut.
Changing the ones digit as well, or changing the wrong digit (56 → 57 for '10 more').
Miscounting on the 100-square by moving diagonally or the wrong direction.
Struggling at decade boundaries because the pattern is memorised without understanding the tens digit's role.
representations: Base-ten tens-rods and ones-cubes (add/remove one rod)
Place-value chart showing only the tens digit changing
Gattegno chart (change the tens-row selection, keep the ones)
authoredAnswer: 66, 46, 83, 30 — produced instantly by changing the tens digit by one, without counting on in ones.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Child reaches 66 but by counting 57, 58 … 66; slow, with fingers.
wrongAnswers.fix: Don't reteach the answer — make the ten visible: add a tens rod on a base-ten mat and show only the tens column changed. Build toward saying it without counting.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Answer differs from the given number by 1, not 10.
wrongAnswers.fix: Contrast 'one more' vs 'ten more' on a base-ten model; ten more adds a ten (tens digit +1), the ones stay put.
